subject: Synthesis for business & technical owners: post-incident summary and verification plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Sun <rebecca@finflow.com>, Samir Patel <samir@finflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident synthesis: high-level summary and next steps

Hi Rebecca / Samir —

Thanks again for the time this morning. I wanted to follow up with a concise synthesis aimed at both your business and technical stakeholders so you have a clear path to verification and acceptance once we've completed the work. This note is intentionally short at the top with a linked technical bundle below.

Executive summary (one line): On 2026-09-14 we experienced a ~3 hour degradation of inference throughput that impacted some of your higher-concurrency endpoints. The immediate customer impact was increased latencies and a small percentage of failed requests during the window.

Key impacts we observed:
- Elevated 95th/99th latency for endpoints using long-context chat flows.
- ~2.8% request error rate spike during the peak window (13:05–15:10 UTC).
- Transient tokenization stalls that caused some in-flight sessions to time out and re-issue requests.

Root-cause (short): An interaction between a batching coalescer regression introduced in the serving runtime (v3.4.1 deploy) and an aggressive autoscaling policy caused repeated KV-cache re-initializations for hot sessions. That combination led to sporadic tokenization stalls and backpressure that cascaded into queue buildup and timeouts.

What we are delivering in this packet:
1) An RCA summary (attached PDF) with timelines and code references.
2) Filtered traces and an event timeline CSV for your verification team.
3) A verification plan with acceptance criteria and required FinFlow checks (listed below).

Proposed short-term mitigations (today → 72 hours):
- Roll back the coalescer change to v3.4.0 for affected pools (complete).
- Pin autoscaler concurrency window to conservative defaults and disable burst scaling for your dedicated pools (in progress).
- Backfill missing KV cache state and rehydrate hot sessions where safe (scheduled).

Proposed medium-term fixes (1–3 weeks):
- Patch the coalescer to respect session affinity and avoid cache eviction when coalescing long-context requests.
- Add an autoscaler safety gate that prevents back-to-back scale-down/up within a 10-minute rolling window.

Verification checklist for FinFlow (what we need from you):
- Validate the attached event_timeline.csv against your client-side logs for 13:00–16:00 UTC on 2026-09-14.
- Confirm a sample of impacted request IDs (we included five in the timeline) against your transaction store.
- If you need slices of audit logs or specific span traces, reply with the request IDs and we will provide redacted extracts.

Attachments: redwood_postincident_summary_v1.pdf, event_timeline_20260914.csv, kv_eviction_trace.snippet.log

Next step: if this summary looks good I’ll share the technical bundle and the official remediation timeline with your security and engineering reviewers. Please let me know if FinFlow requires a compliance-oriented packaging for legal review.

Best,
Logan Wright
Sr. Ops Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Rebecca Sun <rebecca@finflow.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinFlow Legal <legal@finflow.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident synthesis: high-level summary and next steps

Logan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of asks from our side before we start internal verification:

1) Can you provide the exact deploy change (git SHA and diff) for the coalescer regression? Our SREs need code reference to map to client versions.
2) We will need redacted audit log slices with request IDs and timestamps for the five sample IDs you mention. Please include any trace ids that map to duration > 5s.
3) Our legal team asks for a short statement confirming no PII was included in the traces you will share.

Also, can you confirm whether the rollback to v3.4.0 was applied to both US-east and US-west pools for our dedicated capacity?

If you want, I can schedule a 30-minute sync for tomorrow to walk the SREs through the CSV.

—Rebecca
Head of Platform Engineering, FinFlow
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Sun <rebecca@finflow.com>, Samir Patel <samir@finflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident synthesis: high-level summary and next steps

Rebecca — thanks for the questions. Answers below and attached is the technical bundle referenced earlier. I’ve also included a succinct verification plan your SRE and Legal teams can work from.

1) Deploy change details: coalescer regression introduced in commit 7f3c9b2 (pr #1428). The change set is a small loop-level optimization in runtime/batching/coalescer.cc that inadvertently dropped affinity markers when requests included long-context tokens. I’ve pasted the public PR link in the shared Drive (see related_links).

2) Audit slices & traces: we attached kv_eviction_trace.snippet.log and we will provide targeted audit slices for the five sample request IDs in a secure share. We will redact any PII from payloads before delivery.

3) Legal confirmation: Redwood confirms that the traces we will share are redacted and do not contain PII or full user messages. We will provide a short signed attestation if FinFlow legal requires it.

4) Rollback scope: the rollback to v3.4.0 has been applied to both US-east and US-west dedicated pools for FinFlow as of 2026-09-15T22:30:00Z. We left a conservative autoscaler config in place pending the patch.

Verification plan (how Redwood and FinFlow will confirm closure):
A) Redwood provides: filtered traces, timeline CSV, and a small test harness that replays representative requests against the pinned v3.4.0 runtime.
B) FinFlow provides: validation that sample request IDs show equivalent latencies client-side and confirmation that no application-level errors were introduced by request retries.
C) Acceptance criteria: 95th latency returns to baseline within 48 hours of rollback, and observed error rate for the sample IDs drops below 0.5% for a 24-hour window.

If that plan works for you we will:
- Send the redacted audit slices through our secure share by EOD today.
- Schedule the replay window Wednesday 09/17 10:00–11:00 PT (optional for FinFlow to observe).
- Provide a signed attestation for legal if requested.

Attachments: redwood_postincident_summary_v1.pdf, event_timeline_20260914.csv, kv_eviction_trace.snippet.log

Best,
Logan Wright
Sr. Ops Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

On a related note: Marissa and Dylan — please confirm the replay harness parameters are ready and the secure share link is live so I can send to FinFlow.
From: Samir Patel <samir@finflow.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Rebecca Sun <rebecca@finflow.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident synthesis: high-level summary and next steps

Logan / team —

We reviewed the attachments and the timeline. Appreciate the quick rollback and the remediation plan. A few quick confirmations from FinFlow:

- We received the redacted audit slices and verified the five sample request IDs. The timings align with your event_timeline_20260914.csv.
- Our legal team is satisfied with your attestation; please route the signed statement to legal@finflow.com.
- We will join the replay on 09/17 10:00 PT to observe; please send the meeting invite and the replay token.

Once the replay finishes and we confirm the acceptance criteria, we will sign the closure DocuSign envelope. Thanks for the clear synthesis — makes it straightforward to close our internal incident loop.

—Samir
Platform Reliability Lead, FinFlow
